steps.name: canonical-arrival-schema-and-legacy-migration
steps.summary: Established the canonical import/arrival/allocation/receipt schema, migration, canonical incoming loader, ProductVariant references, owner-scoped RLS foundations, immutable source rows, and compatibility RPC baseline. Focused and full tests, Prisma validation, lint, build, and isolated empty legacy-schema migration execution passed in the outer orchestrator. Remaining audited compatibility and behavioral-fixture work is isolated in step 1.

steps.name: canonical-persistence-hardening-and-behavioral-fixture
steps.summary: Hardened canonical manual/CSV creation with an explicit warehouse selector, moved legacy counter synchronization behind a private SECURITY DEFINER trigger boundary, tightened receipt transaction consistency and one-transaction evidence linkage, restored receipt outbox writes, and added the behavioral runner skeleton. Focused/full tests and outer production build passed. Outer audit found the fixture had no representative rows and no psql portability; step 2 owns those acceptance gaps.

steps.name: executable-legacy-migration-proof
steps.summary: Replaced the empty behavioral fixture with two-user representative legacy rows (draft states, repeated variants, deterministic multi-warehouse evidence, and overage), added executable assertions for source/incoming/evidence/RLS/immutability compatibility, and made the proof runner accept a supplied psql or the dedicated Supabase container while preserving target safety. Reworked legacy transaction assignment to link each complete transaction to at most one repeated row and retain deterministic warehouse receipts while recording ambiguous expected remainders. Focused and full tests, Prisma validation, and lint passed. Docker access was denied in this environment, so the disposable-container command could not be executed here; build reached Next font fetch and failed only because the sandbox cannot reach Google Fonts.
